key_ring.holds: the key: 32 raw bytes (here the fixed test key 000102...1f); its fingerprint is sha256 of the bytes
the head checkpoint: JSON {seq, mac, ts}, the last row's seq and MAC and the time it was written; rewritten on every append
an empty lock file, locked while .head is rewritten
the binding: JSON {path}, the canonical store file this key belongs to
an empty lock file, locked while .path is rewritten
the origin anchor: JSON {seq, mac, key_fingerprint}, the first row this machine signed
an empty lock file, locked while .origin is written

name_derivation.examples_note: observed false: each example is the rule computed over the given string as if it were already canonical (the canonicalising function replaced by the identity), not a path observed on that platform
name_derivation.rule: daemon-<first 16 hex of sha256(UTF-8 of the canonical store file path)>.json; the lock, spawn lock and log replace .json with .lock, .spawn.lock, .log. Canonical: realpath, then on POSIX each existing component spelled as its directory lists it where the directory folds case or normalization (_daemon_client.canonical_store_path); on Windows realpath.

placeholders.<digest16>: the first 16 hex digits of sha256 over the scratch store's canonical path (name_derivation shows the rule over fixed paths)
placeholders.<hex64:N>: a 64-hex-digit value the run cannot fix: an HMAC-SHA256 over the store_created row, whose time is the run's clock, or a digest of a file holding it; N numbers distinct values in order of first appearance in the file. The key fingerprint, from the fixed key, stays literal
placeholders.<pid>: the writing process's id (an integer in the file)
placeholders.<scratch>: the run's temporary directory (an absolute path); the path after it is written with / whatever the platform's separator
placeholders.<snapshot_size>: the byte size of the store snapshot (an integer)
placeholders.<timestamp>: an ISO-8601 time on a date within 31 days of the run's clock (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS, optional fraction, Z or offset)

read: Each file: path relative to its root (store: <scratch>/mem, the BETTERMEMORY_DIR; keys: <scratch>/keys, the BETTERMEMORY_KEYS_DIR; the daemon's files: the state directory), mode as an octal string (the mode asked for; POSIX only), and for a text file its exact text with the run's values as placeholders. writers_readers names the components that write and read each. Every JSON text here is written by Python's json.dumps with its default separators (", ", ": "); the state file and the manifest sort their keys, the key ring's files keep the order shown.
setup: _sandbox.world; Store.create(<scratch>/mem/store, keys_dir=<scratch>/keys) with secrets.token_hex answering 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef (the store id) then fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210 (the membership id) and secrets.token_bytes(32) answering the log fixture's KEY_A (bytes 0..31); then daemon._write_daemon_state(<scratch>/state/daemon, store, token 'fixture-token-not-a-secret', port 7397, '127.0.0.1') with the version '0.0.0+fixture'; then create_backup(store file, include_key=True, now=2001-02-03T04:05:06Z) with bettermemory.__version__ = '0.0.0+fixture'.

state_directory_names.note: names only: these files hold host facts (git's config sources, gitdir pins, the machine's id and facts) and are not written by this fixture

timestamp_format.rule: UTC written with Z (never +00:00), seconds, then a fraction of exactly six digits unless the microsecond is 0, when the fraction is left out (Python's datetime.isoformat). The backup's created_at and its head ts are fixed values of the same writer, here without a fraction.

writers_readers.backup: written by backup create; read by backup verify and restore
writers_readers.daemon_state: written by the daemon at start, removed at a clean stop; read by the hook client, the shim and up/down/status, which trust it only after /health?nonce= proves the token
writers_readers.key_ring: written by Store.create, every append (.head), a rekey (.key, .origin) and a store move (.path); read by every opener, security audit and backup
writers_readers.store: written by every opener of the store (daemon, CLI, stdio server); read by the same
